html:
The Ohrid Agreement was signed on 13 August 2001 by the main Macedonian and Albanian parties, ending months of fighting between government forces and Albanian rebels in North Macedonia.

The National Liberation Army, linked to fighters of the Kosovo War, had taken villages near Tetovo and Kumanovo, demanding equal rights for Albanians, about a quarter of the population. Under pressure from the European Union and the United States, the parties agreed that Albanian would be an official language where a fifth of people spoke it, that Albanians would get more police and state jobs, and that local government would gain power. The rebels disarmed under NATO watch. The deal kept North Macedonia together and still shapes its politics.
sum: The Ohrid Agreement was signed on 13 August 2001 by the main Macedonian and Albanian parties, ending months of fighting between government forces and Albanian rebels in North Macedonia.
